incidents.summary: Tate & Lyle sourced sugar from Cambodian plantations associated with forced evictions and human rights abuses, with affected families reaching an out-of-court compensation agreement in 2023.

sources.title: Cambodia: Tate & Lyle settle human rights abuses and land grabs associated with sugar production out of court - Business and Human Rights Centre
sources.quote: Despite such serious allegations, in 2009, KSL won a contract to supply sugar to London-based food and beverage giant Tate & Lyle, who sourced their sugar from these plantations from 2011-2013.

sources.title: 200 Cambodian Families Compensated for Land Seized to Grow Sugar for Tate & Lyle | corpwatch
sources.quote: In 2006, the Cambodian military forcibly evicted some 4,000 villagers who lived in the Chikor Leu commune – whose land fell inside the concessions – to make way for the sugar plantations.

sources.title: Cambodia: Tate & Lyle settle human rights abuses and land grabs associated with sugar production out of court - Business and Human Rights Centre
sources.quote: The NGO Equitable Cambodia announced in April this year that families had reached an out-of-court agreement for an undisclosed financial payment.
